raw.body:
## Summary

Since React 19.2's batched Suspense reveal ("Batching Suspense Boundaries for SSR streaming"), the inline `completeBoundary` runtime (`$RC`) no longer consumes its content segment synchronously — it queues `(boundary, content)` pairs into `$RB` and consumes them in a deferred `revealCompletedBoundaries` (`$RV`) flush (rAF, then a ~300ms/2.3s-LCP throttle). The queued content segment `<div hidden id="S:n">` therefore **stays in the DOM with its id until the flush**.

In a prerender+resume (PPR) document, the resume stream's segment ids are allocated independently of the prerender's, so a resume segment can legally reuse an id the shell already used for a boundary completion — one document containing two `<div hidden id="S:4">` (the shell boundary `B:4`'s completion segment, and the resume segment feeding postponed hole `P:4` via `$RS("S:4","P:4")`). This was safe pre-19.2 **by ordering**: each segment was consumed and removed synchronously by its own inline script before the next same-id segment parsed.

With batching, when the whole document is parsed in one burst (CDN cache hit / fast network / busy main thread delaying rAF), the parser executes `$RS("S:4","P:4")` while the shell's `S:4` is still queued and in the DOM. `completeSegment`'s `document.getElementById("S:4")` returns the **first (wrong) segment** and moves the wrong subtree into the resume hole. The subsequent `$RV` flush then operates on a cross-linked tree and throws:

```
HierarchyRequestError: Failed to execute 'insertBefore' on 'Node': The new child element contains the parent.
```

leaving orphaned never-consumed hidden segments, after which hydration fails (`Minified React error #418` storm — observed 7–38 per load) and React discards the SSR output and client-renders. In the worst observed case the boundary's fallback had already been deleted when the insert threw, leaving a blank region and a pegged main thread (user-facing "Page Unresponsive").

## Environment

- react-dom `19.2.3` (vendored by Next.js `16.2.9`, `cacheComponents: true`, deployed on Vercel — the shell+resume document form)
- Observed on a production e-commerce storefront; browsers: Chromium (headless and desktop), Brave.

## Reproduction

On a captured shell+resume document containing the duplicate-id shape (two `<div hidden id="S:4">` + `$RS("S:4","P:4")` later in the stream):

1. Serve the bytes to the browser **in one burst** (e.g. Playwright `route.fulfill` with the fully buffered body — the deterministic form of a CDN cache-hit delivery).
2. Stock 19.2.3 inline runtime: **10/10 runs corrupt** — instrumented `document.getElementById` shows the `S:4` lookup running with 2 matches present and returning index 0 (the shell's queued segment); then the `HierarchyRequestError` from `$RV`, orphaned `div[hidden][id^="S:"]` nodes, and the #418 storm.
3. Replace **only** the inline `$RC` template with the pre-19.2-style synchronous equivalent (same per-pair logic `$RV` runs — fallback walk, child move, `"$"` reveal, `_reactRetry` — applied at script-execution time): **0/10 corrupt**, all segments consumed, clean hydration.

Over a real network the failure is timing-dependent (~2/3 of hard loads on a fast connection in our measurements; a dribbled stream lets the rAF flush win the race), which is why it presents as a flaky production-only hydration failure.

I'm happy to provide the captured HTML documents, the instrumentation snippets, and to work on a minimal standalone repro if useful.

## Suggested direction

Resumed streams' segment/placeholder ids must not be able to collide with ids the shell's queued completions still hold in the DOM. Options that would each fix it:

- distinct id namespace (or prefix) for resume segments, or
- `completeSegment` (`$RS`) flushing the pending `$RB` queue before its lookup, or
- boundary completions removing the queued segment from the id space at queue time (e.g. clearing its `id` when pushed to `$RB`).

## Note

Filed with a cross-reference in vercel/next.js, since the colliding document shape is produced by Next's PPR prerender+resume path, but the ordering regression itself is in the 19.2 fizz inline runtime.
raw.title: Bug: 19.2 batched Suspense reveal can consume the wrong completion segment when a resumed (PPR) stream reuses a queued segment id — DOM corruption + hydration failure
